- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, reduce forecasted overshoots and avoid overreacting to short-term spikes.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25) and prices are trending upward, cap upward forecasts to prevent overcorrection.  
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust by adding a small upward bias to prevent premature mean reversion.  
- In absence of strong sentiment signals, model overestimates mean price — apply a downward bias of 0.5–1.5% relative to recent 7-day average.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows strong upward momentum (e.g., >5% daily gain for 3+ days), reduce forecasted peak lag by 1–2 days.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00) and history shows volatility, model tends to overpredict volatility — dampen forecast variance by 10–20%.
